prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the development of long-acting incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I change my third name from Mojsov to Knudsen, and I want that change made explicitly. The case for B023 itself is unchanged: a specific, nameable discovery chain from proglucagon processing and incretin physiology to long-acting agonists, a clear change in the field, a stable mechanism, and a decade or more of independent outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal disease. Delay has a real cost because the laureates are living. What moved me is the chair's first question. Priority for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide among Mojsov, Habener and Bell cannot be settled from the record we have, and I said in round 1 that unresolved priority is a poor basis for a seat. Without it, my preference for Mojsov rested on a contested claim, while Knudsen's contribution, the acylation and albumin-binding design that gave the peptide a half-life of days, is documented, specific and is the step that made the biology a medicine. Drucker and Holst remain the physiological core. I accept the broader citation, physiology plus long-acting therapy, because the prize can reasonably say that this discovery became a treatment. I still hold that the physiology comes first in the citation and the product is the evidence of importance, not the object of the prize.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still attribution. Three names cannot carry Drucker, Holst, Knudsen and Mojsov, and by dropping Mojsov I leave the peptide-identification story with a gap, with Habener and Bell also outside the credited names. A reviewer could say the prize favours a company and rewards optimisation over discovery, and could reasonably ask why a development scientist takes a seat that an academic discoverer of the active peptide might claim. If the committee concluded that the discovery, not the drug, is the object of the prize, my new trio would be the weaker one. Pairing with a second part would also be hard, because B001 has six claimants for three places and B022 omits Eshhar, so I do not see a partner that fits the three-person cap this year.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, rests the third seat on Knudsen's acylation and albumin-binding work as what made the peptide a drug, and notes that the trio changes if the committee decides the prize rewards discovery rather than drug design.
responses.response: In round 1 I argued that identification of the active peptide is upstream of every analogue, and I still think that logic is sound in principle. But you ask for a decision, and the decision turns on evidence we do not have: nothing in the supplied record lets us apportion priority among Mojsov, Habener and Bell. I would not spend a seat on a claim I cannot defend in a citation. I therefore move to your trio. I do so on the basis that the physiology leads the citation and that Knudsen's work is a discovery-level step with a nameable mechanism, not on the basis that five colleagues named her. I accept your caveat that if the committee defined the prize as discovery only, the trio would change.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved Knudsen into his trio in place of Mojsov after rereading colleagues' ballots, arguing that acylated long-acting design is at the core of the achievement and not an industrial afterthought, and keeps B051 as the first alternative.
responses.response: I follow your move, and I now agree with it, although for a more limited reason than yours. You say the design of long-acting analogues lies at the core. I would say it is the step that closes the chain from physiology to medicine, and the citation should keep the order of those two. On B051 my view is as before: Mori and Walter are a clean pairing and the science is mature, but its disease-level consequence is still mostly correlative, so I would not place it as a second part in the same year as a decisive clinical recognition. Your reservation on Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck for B001 is also the reason I keep that ballot as an alternative and do not propose it as a second part.

responses.point: El Manira names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, wants the configuration to carry both the physiology and the drug, and says that an unresolved Mojsov priority and a company-based laureate are both costs that he cannot resolve from the evidence.
responses.response: We now agree on the trio and on a citation that carries both halves. I share your discomfort with the company-based scientist and with leaving out Mojsov, and I do not think either can be eliminated. I weigh them differently from you in one respect. You treat the Mojsov question as a possible reason to displace Knudsen or Holst if it proves decisive. I would not displace Holst, since his work on secretion and action is the base of the physiology, and I would not reopen the question without new documentary evidence on who first identified and characterised the truncated peptide. In your round-1 text you also doubt that a three-name solution can be forced for B001. I agree, and I regard that as the main reason a split prize is not available this year.

responses.point: Sandberg argues that a single-achievement prize avoids splitting credit across unrelated fields, that the third seat depends on how the core achievement is defined, and ranks B051 and B028 as alternatives.
responses.response: I agree that the third seat depends on how we define the core achievement, and I have now defined it as the physiology and the long-acting therapy together, which puts Knudsen in the third seat. I also agree with you that a single part is cleaner than a split with an unrelated field. On B028 I keep the reservation I gave in round 1: the 2008 prize recognised the HPV and cervical cancer link, the virus-like-particle step reads as a continuation, and the Zhou priority question is unresolved. I do not consider it ready to be paired with B023 now. If the committee does want a second part, the order of my alternatives for that purpose would be B001 and B022, both of which have attribution problems that I do not think we can fix by a vote.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius supports Drucker, Holst and Knudsen with a citation pairing physiology and long-acting therapy, and adds that long-term safety of the incretin class beyond weight and glucose is still being defined.
responses.response: I agree with the trio and the broad shape of your citation. Your point on long-term safety is the one nobody else raised, and I think it is worth recording. I do not think it weakens maturity. The effects on glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes are established across independent trials, and safety questions of this kind follow most drug classes without invalidating the discovery. It does argue for keeping the citation on the physiology and the established indications, naming type 2 diabetes and obesity and not claiming wider benefits that are still being studied. My wording does that.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a company-based development scientist alongside two academic discoverers, or will decide that the prize should reward the physiological discovery only, which would restore Mojsov.

Priority for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide among Mojsov, Habener and Bell. I cannot resolve it from the supplied record, and my decision to leave Mojsov out rests on that lack of evidence and not on a finding against her claim.
Whether any second achievement can fit the three-person cap with a defensible credit. B001 has six claimants and B022 omits Eshhar, so I have not proposed a second part.
statement.conflict_note: No candidate-specific conflict or recusal need arises for B023, B001 or B022. My prior co-authorship with Ronald Evans concerns nuclear receptors, and Evans is not among the credited names on the shortlist. My research on nuclear receptors and dopamine neurons is in a different field from every shortlisted achievement. My shared Karolinska affiliation and past co-authorship with committee colleagues, including a 2009 paper with El Manira and about twenty works with Svenningsson, are not ties to any shortlisted candidate, and no recusal is proposed.
